Story & Plot

Set in present-day Punjab, Rehmat presents three interconnected stories adapted from short stories by acclaimed author Ajeet Cour. The narrative follows a woman who secretly shelters a wounded stranger in her home while his family endures grief and difficult choices. Meanwhile, a mysterious elderly man arrives in a village and calls himself God.

Comedy & Entertainment

As a drama centering on grief, modern conflict, and traditional compassion in Punjab, the film does not focus on humor or traditional comedic relief. Its entertainment value relies instead on its expansive narrative and tranquil picture of India's storied region. The tone remains serious and contemplative throughout its runtime.

Performances & Direction

The film features a talented cast including Naseeruddin Shah, Mita Vashisht, Suvinder Vicky, Diya Kamboj, and Harwinder Singh Aujla. Reviewers specifically highlight Naseeruddin Shah, noting that he shines and successfully reclaims the plurality of Punjab in Gurvinder Singh's poignant portrait.

Strengths

  • Poignant portrait of Punjab's plurality
  • Strong central performances led by Naseeruddin Shah
  • Thoughtful adaptation of Ajeet Cour's short stories
  • Quiet tussle between traditional compassion and modern conflict

Weaknesses

While the film offers a tranquil and striking picture of its setting, its expansive narrative and quiet tone may test the patience of viewers looking for faster pacing. The interconnected stories also run the risk of feeling slightly dispersed across its 157-minute runtime.

Final verdict

Gurvinder Singh's Rehmat is a poignant and tranquil drama that brings the plurality of Punjab to the screen with the help of a stellar cast. It serves as an antidote to fractured times through its exploration of traditional compassion versus modern conflict. Recommended for viewers who appreciate thoughtful, character-driven international cinema.
